    1-2

    Lecture 1-2

    How do the simulator's numbers become evidence you can argue with?

    Lecture 1-2 · the plan

    From trends to an evidence register

    1. Three pulls from the tabrun, snapshot and event log, each tagged with a role
    2. The route without the tabCSV export from the OTS, then drop it in the workbook
    3. Reading the TE-1 trendswhich tags moved, when, and in what order
    4. Fact, inference or opinionsorting what you measured from what you were told

    From this OTS (live)

    Three pulls, three kinds of evidence

    The workbook is set up. Its first job is to bring the simulator in as evidence.

    Run

    Every distributed control system (DCS) trend, in time.

    Snapshot

    Every reading now, beside its design value.

    Event log

    Alarms, trips, actions, phone answers.

    Each pull is a comma-separated values (CSV) dataset with a role: Initial run, Plant test or Fix.

    In the tab

    One button, three datasets

    • Pick the role first, then Pull all three.
    • Pull again after each plant test and after the fix.
    • In the student edition the log hides the instructor's fault lines.

    Standalone copies

    Export from the OTS, drop into the workbook

    Interactive — real TE-1 run

    Which tag moved first?

    The valve opens while the steam falls; at 23 min it is wide open and the outlet temperature drops.

    Evidence register

    The workbook drafts the evidence lines

    • Suggest evidence turns a dataset into lines: deviations, on-design readings, alarms, changes.
    • On-design readings feed IS / IS NOT: where the problem is, and where it could be but is not.
    • You keep, edit or delete each line.

    Interactive — sort each statement

    Fact, inference or opinion?

    A computed number is an inference: it is only as good as the instruments behind it.

    1-3

    Lecture 1-3

    TE-1, part 1: what exactly is wrong, and what could cause it?

    Lecture 1-3 · the plan

    Engage, Define, Explore on a real run

    1. The case as the board sees itExample 1.1: TE-1 after 35 minutes, no action taken
    2. Engageis it time-critical, and what do we tell people
    3. Definea problem statement that names no cause, and IS / IS NOT
    4. Explorea heat balance on E-301 tells which instruments to trust
    5. Hypotheses screenedS / D / N against the evidence leaves four standing

    Example 1.1 · problem statement · read first

    EXAMPLE 1.1TE-1 · Boil-up falling, steam valve wide open

    Situation given

    “Unit lined out. Production reports the rate has been drifting down this shift.” You load TE-1 in the OTS and let it run 35 minutes without touching anything; the table shows the board at 0:35.

    (a) Decide whether it is time-critical. (b) Write the problem statement and the IS / IS NOT table. (c) Check which instruments you can trust, then list and screen hypotheses.

    TagDesign0:35
    TIC-301 OUT (TV-301), %54.899.9
    FI-304 LP steam, t/h5.193.65
    TIC-301 heater outlet, °C66.0064.66
    FI-401 boil-up, t/h6.955.26
    FIC-101 feed, t/h26.3925.35
    PIC-202 vacuum, kPa a13.5013.53
    PIC-202 OUT (air bleed), %50.177.8
    FIC-302 circulation, t/h900900
    TI-303 heater inlet, °C61.7061.58
    Alarms 0:00–0:35—none

    TIC = temperature controller, FI = flow indicator, LP = low-pressure steam (3.5 bar a). Values from the seeded TE-1 run.

    Stage 1 · Engage

    EXAMPLE 1.1Time-critical? Not yetstep 1 of 6

    ConsequenceAt risk?Why
    SafetyNovacuum, level and S all inside limits
    EnvironmentNonothing leaves that should not
    EquipmentNocirculation normal, 900 t/h
    ProductionYesboil-up 24 % low, crystals follow
    Decision: keep running and investigate. Stop line: FI-401 below 4.5 t/h.

    Stage 2 · Define

    EXAMPLE 1.1A statement that names no causestep 2 of 6

    E-301 passes only 3.65 t/h of LP steam with TV-301 fully open and cannot hold 66 °C, against 5.19 t/h at 55 % normally, since about 0:23; boil-up 5.26 t/h.

    “Scaled heater” would be a cause; it stays out.

    Stage 2 · Define

    EXAMPLE 1.1IS / IS NOT kills whole familiesstep 3 of 6

    The vacuum is not short: PIC-202 is on set point with the bleed opening wider.

    Stage 3 · Explore

    EXAMPLE 1.1A heat balance on E-301step 4 of 6

    Before trusting any cause, check the instruments: steam side and liquor side must carry the same heat.

    $Q$
    heat passed by E-301 to the circulating liquor
    kW
    $\dot m_s$
    LP steam condensed, read on FI-304
    kg/s
    $\lambda$
    latent heat of steam at 3.5 bar a (steam tables)
    kJ/kg
    $F_c$
    circulation through E-301, read on FIC-302
    kg/s
    $c_p$
    heat capacity of the liquor, fitted at design
    kJ/(kg·K)
    $T_{Fc},\,T_{mix}$
    heater outlet (TIC-301) and inlet (TI-303)
    °C
    $$Q=\dot m_s\,\lambda=F_c\,c_p\,(T_{Fc}-T_{mix})$$

    Stage 3 · Explore

    EXAMPLE 1.1Fit $c_p$ where everything is knownstep 5 of 6

    From the previous slide$Q=\dot m_s\,\lambda=F_c\,c_p\,(T_{Fc}-T_{mix})$
    $Q_0=\dfrac{5.195\times 1000}{3600}\times 2148=3100\ \text{kW}$steam side at design, t/h converted to kg/s
    $c_p=\dfrac{3100}{250.1\times(66.00-61.70)}=2.88\ \text{kJ/(kg K)}$liquor side carries the same heat

    Assumes no heat loss and constant $c_p$ between design and the upset.

    Stage 3 · Explore

    EXAMPLE 1.1At 0:35 the two sides still agreestep 6 of 6

    Heat balance and fitted $c_p$ = 2.88$Q=\dot m_s\,\lambda=F_c\,c_p\,(T_{Fc}-T_{mix})$
    $Q_s=\dfrac{3.646\times 1000}{3600}\times 2148=2175\ \text{kW}$steam side from FI-304
    $Q_l=250.1\times 2.88\times(64.66-61.58)=2219\ \text{kW}$liquor side from FIC-302, TIC-301, TI-303

    Within 2 %: FT-304 and TT-301 tell the truth; the heater gives 70 % of design heat at 100 % valve.

    Interactive — move the readings

    Do the instruments agree?

    Stage 3 balance$\dot m_s\,\lambda=F_c\,c_p\,(T_{Fc}-T_{mix})$
    Steam side
    Liquor side
    Gap

    When both sides agree the instruments are fine: the heater itself passes less heat.

    Stage 3 · Explore

    EXAMPLE 1.1Seven hypotheses on six branches

    Each idea becomes a working hypothesis (WH-n) with an “if … then we should observe” and a falsifier.

    Interactive — click a cell: S, D, N

    Screen the hypotheses against the evidence

    S supports, D denies, N neutral. Before the tests four causes survive; one D is enough to kill a cause.

    Lecture 1-3 · summary

    What section 1-3 settled

    • TE-1 costs production, not safety: keep running and investigate.
    • The statement names the symptom with numbers, never a cause.
    • The heat balance proves the instruments before any hypothesis.
    • S / D / N leaves four causes that only tests can separate.

    1-4

    Lecture 1-4

    TE-1, part 2: which test settles it, what fix, and what do we keep?

    Lecture 1-4 · the plan

    Plan, Do it, Look back, hand in

    1. Two tests with predictionsa Look test and a Change test that split the four survivors
    2. Do itresults, the fix, and actual against predicted
    3. The cost ledgerwhat the diagnosis cost and what the fix is worth
    4. Look back and hand inthe training rule, a barrier, the report and the .woods.json

    Example 1.2 · problem statement · read first

    EXAMPLE 1.2TE-1 continued · split the survivors and fix

    Example 1.1: TE-1 at 0:35: TV-301 at 100 %, FI-304 3.65 t/h (design 5.19), boil-up 5.26 t/h (6.95), no alarm; heat balance closes within 2 %.

    Four working hypotheses (WH) survive: WH-1 E-301 tubes scaled; WH-2 LP steam header pressure low; WH-3 TV-301 not following its output; WH-5 condensate backing up in the shell.

    (a) Plan one Look test and one Change test, with predictions, stop and back-out rules. (b) Run them in the OTS and judge each WH. (c) Choose the fix; compare actual with predicted. (d) Close the cost ledger.

    Stage 4 · Plan

    EXAMPLE 1.2Predict before you movestep 1 of 5

    Four survivors share one signature. A test is worth running only where their predictions differ.

    TestMoveIf WH-1If WH-2If WH-3
    T-1 Lookphone utilities; read TI-301Lheader normalheader < 3.5 bar aheader normal
    T-2 Changeopen HV-306 for 10 minFI-304 staysFI-304 staysFI-304 rises

    WH-5 predicts as WH-1; the fix decides it. Stop rule: close HV-306 if TIC-301 > 68 °C.

    Interactive — real T-2 run

    Bypass open: did the steam rise?step 2 of 5

    HV-306 open from 0:40 to 0:50 (shaded). FI-304 before , after .

    More valve area added no steam: the valve was not the limit, the heater was. WH-3 dies, WH-1 stands.

    Stage 5 · Do it

    EXAMPLE 1.2The workbook judges each teststep 3 of 5

    • T-1: header 3.5 bar a, TI-301L 64.6 °C = TIC-301: WH-2 and WH-4 killed.
    • T-2: FI-304 3.61 → 3.64 t/h, within noise: WH-3 killed.

    Stage 5 · Do it

    EXAMPLE 1.2Wash out E-301, then comparestep 4 of 5

    • Wash-out at 0:55; TIC-301 back on 66 °C at 1:02:40.
    • At 1:30: TV-301 55 %, FI-304 5.23, FI-401 6.94 t/h. All four predictions met.
    • The trap was untouched, so WH-5 dies too.

    Stage 4 → 6 · the ledger

    EXAMPLE 1.2What it cost, what it is worthstep 5 of 5

    $$V=\Delta\dot P\times 24\times d\times p$$
    $\Delta\dot P$
    crystals lost while scaled, 2.12 t/h (boil-up 24 % low × 8.72 t/h)
    t/h
    $d$
    days until the next planned stop (assumed 14)
    d
    $p$
    price of ammonium sulphate crystals (assumed 200)
    USD/t

    $V$ = USD 142 134 recovered against USD 5 825 spent (diagnosis 40, T-2 50, wash-out 5 735).

    Interactive — change the assumptions

    Wash out now, or run on?

    From the previous slide$V=\Delta\dot P\times 24\times d\times p$
    Value recovered
    Spent
    Net

    The wash-out pays back within a day; waiting for the next stop is the expensive choice.

    Stage 6 · Look back

    Keep the rule, add a barrier

    The plant is back. What stops the next scaling from costing a shift?

    Training rule: if TIC-301 OUT is at 100 % and FI-304 falls with the header normal, E-301 is scaling: plan the wash-out.
    $$k=\frac{\text{FI-304}}{\text{TIC-301 OUT}}\quad 0.095\ \rightarrow\ 0.037\ \text{t/h per \%}$$

    New alarm: TIC-301 OUT > 85 % for 10 min; wash out when $k$ falls below 0.07.

    Lecture 1-4 · summary

    What section 1-4 settled

    • Look tests first, then one Change test whose predictions differ.
    • T-1 killed WH-2 and WH-4, T-2 killed WH-3, the fix killed WH-5.
    • The ledger: USD 5 825 spent, about USD 142 000 recovered.
    • Keep a rule and a barrier; hand in the .woods.json and report.

    Can you solve it yourself?

    Class activity · the plan

    Two cases, situation text only

    TE-1 was solved for you. Now the same method on cases whose answers you do not have.

    1. Problem 1.1 · TE-2Stage 0 to the problem statement: pulls, urgency, IS / IS NOT (practises 1-2 and 1-3)
    2. Problem 1.2 · TE-3hypotheses, S / D / N and a two-test plan with predictions (practises 1-3 and 1-4)

    Work in teams of four: leader, OTS operator, recorder, devil's advocate. Save the .woods.json at the end.

    Problem 1.1 · statement · read first

    PROBLEM 1.1TE-2 · Pressure high in the afternoon

    Situation given

    “Unit lined out. The day is getting hot; PIC-202 is creeping up and the air bleed is nearly shut.”

    Load TE-2 on Exercises and let it run 30 minutes without acting. In the workbook:

    (a) pull the run, the snapshot and the event log with role Initial run; (b) fill 0.2 and 0.4 with numbers and times; (c) decide in 1.3–1.4 whether it is time-critical; (d) write the IS / IS NOT table and the problem statement 2.11, naming no cause.

    Problem 1.1 · how to set it up

    PROBLEM 1.1Run it, pull it, define it

    StepWhereReport
    Load TE-2, run 30 minExercisestime of each change
    Pull all threelive cardrole Initial run
    Suggest evidenceeach datasetdeviations, on-design
    Engage, DefineStages 1–2urgency, IS / IS NOT, 2.11

    Done when 2.11 is one sentence with numbers and no cause.

    Problem 1.2 · statement · read first

    PROBLEM 1.2TE-3 · Product getting finer

    Situation given

    “The centrifuge house complains the cake drains badly; AIT-206 has been falling for three hours. Nobody changed any set point.”

    Load TE-3; it opens with three hours of history. In the workbook:

    (a) pull the data including the history; (b) build the fishbone with at least one idea per branch and five hypotheses with “if … then” and a falsifier; (c) screen them with S / D / N; (d) plan one Look and one Change test with predictions, stop and back-out rules; (e) run the tests and judge each hypothesis.

    Problem 1.2 · how to set it up

    PROBLEM 1.2Hypotheses first, tests second

    StepWhereReport
    History and trendsTrend explorer, 3 h windowwhich tag moved first, and when
    Fishbone, WH list3.4 and 3.6≥ 5 hypotheses, six branches
    S / D / N4.3survivors and why
    Tests4.6, then 5.0predictions, results, verdicts

    A test is useful only if two survivors predict different results.

    Before you go

    Key Takeaways

    1

    Pull run, snapshot and log with a role, after every move.

    2

    State the symptom with numbers; name no cause in 2.11.

    3

    Prove the instruments with a balance before any hypothesis.

    4

    Choose tests whose predictions differ between survivors.

    5

    Close the ledger and keep one rule and one barrier.
